feeds.title: The History Blog
feeds.description: Hello, I am Livius. I created this history blog page because my interests are primarily European ancient and medieval. Here I am providing general blogs on history, historical podcasts, historical illustrations, ancient books, and many more. I also intend to make a note of all the topically relevant books I read, and a list of all the topically relevant books sitting in a pile glaring at me.

feeds.title: Thuppahi's Blog » European History
feeds.description: Thuppahi's Blog features the latest articles about European history. He talks about interventions of Michel Roberts in the public realm with reference to Sri Lankan political affairs. Roberts was educated at St. Aloysius College in Galle and the universities of Peradeniya and Oxford. He taught History at Peradeniya University and Anthropology at Adelaide university. He is now retired and lives in Adelaide.

feeds.title: A Corner of Tenth-Century Europe
feeds.description: This blog contains occasional musings, by me, Jonathan Jarrett, M. A. (Cantab.), Ph. D. (Lond.), for whatever may be occupying my mind on matters medieval and so forth which is usually early medievalist thoughts and ponderings. I am a lecturer in medieval history and like to talk and write about it passionately.

feeds.title: History@Kingston » European History
feeds.description: Gather news and views from the history department archives at Kingston University, London. History@Kingston is a multi-authored blog written by staff, students, alumni, and public historians who contribute to the study of history at Kingston University and the town's rich local heritage. We also occasionally host special guest blogs authored by experts beyond Kingston.

feeds.title: EUSTORY History Campus Blog
feeds.description: A blog where young authors from all over Europe regularly publish posts about current events, discuss the relevance of historical anniversaries, and share their personal approaches to issues related to history and identity in Europe. The EUSTORY History Campus gives voice to personal stories and perspectives on the history and identity of young Europeans.

feeds.title: Cambridge University Press » European History
feeds.description: The Official Blog of Cambridge University Press showcases reflections on European History, Military, Literature, The rise of Capitalism, Nazism, and more. Featuring current news and commentary from Cambridge authors and staff, fifteeneightyfour is dedicated to sharing scholarship from the finest academics in the world and fostering discussion worldwide about important issues in culture, politics, and science.

feeds.title: Eurohistory
feeds.description: The European Royal History Journal is the original creation of Arturo E. Beéche, who is also the publisher and editor of Eurohistory. Along with Seth Leonard, The Eurohistory blog publishes accounts and fascinating accounts and snippets from European Royal History. Both contributors to this blog are passionate about history.

feeds.title: Yale Books Blog » European History
feeds.description: Yale Books is the official blog for Yale University Press London. The purpose of this blog is to enhance cultural life and educate people by sharing books, news, and events for the UK. Yale University Press is a university press linked with Yale University. It publishes articles on European History, Politics, Current Affairs, Architecture, Biography, Fashion, and many more.

feeds.title: Historical Easter Eggs Today in History Blog » European History
feeds.description: Today in History is a blog page that shares historical knowledge on Europe by sharing posts about European History written by Cape Cod Curmudgeon. The page contains a number of categories including; European History, Art History, Asian History, Canadian History, and many more.

feeds.title: Rechtsgeschiedenis » European history
feeds.description: Otto Vervaart's blog about legal history and history from perspectives touching on legal history. Otto here. On this blog, I like to present news concerning legal history, and news from the perspective of legal history. Here I post about European history and Legal history from a Dutch view.

feeds.title: Europe Across Borders
feeds.description: Europe Across Borders is a blog page that advances historical knowledge on Europe by sharing information on current research projects and discussing contemporary issues. The blog offers dynamic and innovative explorations of European history and provides historical context to modern controversies, bridging the past with the present.

feeds.title: European Royal History
feeds.description: This blog will mainly focus on the past but I will deliver current news about both the reigning and non-reigning royal families in Europe. The author of this blog has had an interest in European royalty since the late 1970s. My main interest is in British Royalty but I am also interested in all the monarchies of Europe past and present.

feeds.title: UNC Press Blog » European History
feeds.description: Find comprehensive, engaging articles on Medieval and European History at the University of North Carolina Press's official blog. The University of North Carolina Press advances the research, teaching, and public service missions of a great public university by publishing excellent work from leading scholars, writers, and intellectuals and by presenting that work to both academic audiences and general readers.

feeds.title: The Library Of Congress Blog » European History
feeds.description: In the European History category of our blog, find articles that educate about European Origins and all of the fascinating histories of Europe. Library of Congress provides access to and engages you in your intellectual and creative endeavors with millions of books, films and video, audio recordings, photographs, newspapers, scripts, geography, and maps contained in its collections.
